_comment: Canonical pace_delta -> label truth table.
Read by BOTH halves of the codebase so the Swift and Python wordings
cannot drift silently:
- app/GradusKit/Tests/GradusKitTests/PaceLabelTests.swift (Swift)
- tests/test_ui.py::PaceLabelTruthTableTests              (Python)
It lives inside the SwiftPM test target for the same reason as
signal-levels.json in this directory -- see that file's header.
Deliberately does not cover the missing-value case: the TUI renders
that as "n/a" and Mac/iOS render it as "pace unavailable", a
pre-existing difference this fixture does not attempt to unify. It also
keeps every case strictly outside both surfaces' 'on pace' band --
the TUI's is +/-5 points and Mac/iOS's is +/-1 point, deliberately
different -- except pace_delta 0.0, which is on-pace under either rule.
Only the wording once a surface decides to show a number is shared.
The 0.125 / -0.125 rows exist specifically to catch a rounding-mode
mismatch: Python's `round()` builtin ties to even (round(12.5) == 12),
while Swift's `Double.rounded()` ties away from zero (12.5 rounds to
13). Both language implementations round half away from zero -- Python
spells it out explicitly since its builtin does not -- so these rows
must both come out as 13 points, not 12.

cases.label: on pace
cases.why: Exactly on schedule -- on-pace under either surface's band.

cases.label: 6% behind
cases.why: Just past the TUI's on-pace band edge (+/-5 points); both surfaces show a number here.

cases.label: 13% ahead
cases.why: Rounding-mode boundary: 12.5 points rounds away from zero to 13, not to even (12).

cases.label: 150% ahead
cases.why: pace_delta is not clamped (INV-4); an extreme value must still format, not crash or truncate.

cases.label: 100% behind
cases.why: Large behind-schedule value at a round number.
